narrative: Post-fire recovery and nutrient cycling feature strongly this week, with a 35-year chronosequence showing aboveground nitrogen pools still growing after stand-replacing fire while surface pools remain unchanged, and a companion test of the subsurface nitrogen bank hypothesis in northern conifer forests. Under the climate theme, a widespread desert plant recovered better from extreme desiccation under humid air and elevated CO2, karst vegetation showed amplified phenological responses to climate variability, and a Nature Climate Change study found that high wind speed reduces water use efficiency across terrestrial ecosystems. In movement and behaviour, step selection was used to predict connectivity from GPS trajectories, and individual boldness was shown to structure encounters in a rodent community. Conservation papers highlighted a global meta-analysis of river barrier removal, where recovery extends well beyond the first year, and joint species distribution modelling to guide American chestnut restoration. Invasion work included a horizon scan of high-risk non-native species for the Canary Islands, while evolution papers showed urban adaptation in white clover varies with biogeographic origin. On the methods side, new tools include the fishmax R package, ITSxRust for long-read fungal amplicons, and a Bayesian dynamic mixing model for isotopic diet estimation.
